reconstructed_theorem_text: For every complete real inner-product space E equipped with an arbitrary measurable-space structure, every measure mu on E, and every nonzero real eta, the following holds for all y,yprime,x in E. Put Z_y = integral exp(-norm(z-y)^2/(2*eta)) dmu(z) and Z_yprime = integral exp(-norm(z-yprime)^2/(2*eta)) dmu(z). Define the real-valued function H(t) = -norm(t-y)^2/(2*eta)-log(Z_y)-(-norm(t-yprime)^2/(2*eta))+log(Z_yprime). Then its gradient at x, taken with respect to the given real inner product and the spatial variable t, equals eta^(-1) times (y-yprime). The displayed function is genuinely Frechet differentiable, and this gradient identity holds at every x. Both integral-logarithm terms are scalar constants in t, interpreted using the Lean real integral and logarithm. No finite-dimensionality, Borel compatibility, sigma-finiteness, probability normalization, integrability or positivity of the normalizers, or positivity of eta is assumed. Negative nonzero eta is allowed.
